chunks: If you refuse except to claim that I erred and went astray,

why do you lead astray the general public of the Ummah of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) by my misguidance, and hold them accountable for my error, and declare them disbelievers on account of my sins!
Your swords are on your shoulders; you place them in places of purity and disease, and you mix up the one who sinned with the one who did not sin.
And you know that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stoned the adulterer [the married one], then he prayed over him, then he allowed his family to inherit from him,

and he killed the murderer and allowed his family to inherit his estate, and he cut off the thief and whipped the unmarried adulterer, then he distributed to both of them from the booty, and they married Muslim women;

so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) took them to task for their sins, and established Allah's right in them, and did not withhold their share from Islam, nor did he remove their names from among His people.

key_terms.أُمَّةِ مُحَمَّدٍ: Ummah of Muhammad (the community of the Prophet)

ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad handle the sins of individuals without excluding them from Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) critiques the Kharijites for their error of generalizing individual sins to the entire community, a practice he illustrates by noting that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) applied specific punishments like stoning or cutting to sinners without excluding them from the fold of Islam or their inheritance rights. This argument underscores the Shia principle of distinguishing between *dhanb* (sin) and *kufr* (disbelief), emphasizing that major sins do not necessarily constitute apostasy unless accompanied by denial of core tenets.
